headline: Today's short easy run at your lowest HR of the recent block reinforces a settled aerobic base as volume holds flat.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Today was a short, controlled easy effort — the lowest heart rate of the recent runs at a comfortable pace, sitting right in line with the improved efficiency picture that's been consistent for a couple of weeks now. Nothing here changes the story: the aerobic engine is running well and comparable-effort heart rate remains meaningfully lower than the prior period. This is confirmation, not new information.

The pattern you should notice is that the block has now flattened. Volume is essentially unchanged from the prior four weeks, and the recent runs remain moderate in distance, low in elevation, and single-day. With the St. Olavsleden crossing about a month out — a self-supported, pack-loaded, moderately mountainous multi-day effort — the gap between what you're training and what the event demands is the most relevant thing on the table. Your aerobic efficiency and strength base are clearly intact, so this isn't a fitness concern; it's a specificity one. The durability qualities that event will test — loaded carries, consecutive-day time on feet, sustained climbing — still haven't entered the block.
watch_items: Whether pack-loaded or back-to-back efforts appear in the coming weeks, given how close the crossing now is.
Whether per-run elevation starts climbing to rehearse sustained uphill/downhill terrain rather than staying flat.
Whether the steady strength frequency is maintained or deliberately tapered as event-specific durability work is introduced.

evidence_items.text: ▼ Easy-run HR averaging 143 bpm vs 155 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 7 runs)
▲ 4-week volume 136 km vs 133 km prior block (+2%)
